96909.title: Display switcher offers List, Tech View and Board View and marks the active one
96909.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field. To add one:
    • Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name (e.g. Esther Howard), an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 led by Esther Howard, S1-352 with no lead):
    • Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and the Asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Save. The example customer and unit are not on the test site, so create them first: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, TRK-118) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples; on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581").
    • Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (e.g. Esther Howard); it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
96909.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top navigation.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Look at the display switcher at the right of the toolbar and hover each of its buttons.
  4. Write down the label or tooltip of each button and which one is highlighted.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  6. Look at which switcher button is highlighted now.
  7. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  8. Look at which switcher button is highlighted now.
  9. In the display switcher, click List (tooltip "List").
96909.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The switcher offers exactly three display options: List, Tech View and Board View.
  • Only the option you are viewing is highlighted: List at the start, Tech View after step 5, Board View after step 7, List again after step 9.
  • Write down the words you see on each button or tooltip. The design's tooltips read "Table", "By Lead Tech" and "Board". A different label alone is not a fail (the wording is an open product question), but a missing option or no highlight is.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-R1, S1-R9, read 8 Oct 2026. Design: Claude Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html), toolbar view switch (aria-label "View"); on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R1: “The Work Orders toolbar offers List, Tech View, and Board View display options.”
  • S1-R9: “The switcher visually indicates the active display option.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

97033.custom_preconds:
1. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (the display switcher only shows at 1024 px and wider).
  3. You can open Google Analytics for the property the QA build reports to, at Admin > DebugView. The QA build runs analytics in debug mode, so each event appears in DebugView within a few seconds under your user. If you cannot open DebugView, the event checks in this case cannot be done by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see on the Work Orders page.
  4. Four test users at this location with Work Orders view (Settings > Staff): U1, U2 and U3 with see financial data, U4 without.
  5. You can open the Story 12 field selection report in Google Analytics (built and kept by Milos Vasic).
  6. Do the steps on two different days of the same week (Monday to Sunday).
97033.custom_steps:
1. Day 1: sign in as U1, open Work Orders > Board View > the Fields to display menu, turn VIN/Serial on, then off, then on again.
  2. Day 2: sign in as U2 and turn VIN/Serial on in Board View.
  3. Day 2: sign in as U3, open Board View and turn Total price off.
  4. Day 2: sign in as U4 and open Board View (change nothing).
  5. After the week, open the field selection report for Board View for that week, filtered to these four users if the report allows.
97033.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • VIN/Serial: 4 users saw it (U1 to U4) and 2 have it on (U1, U2), so the rate is 2 ÷ 4 = 50%. U1 counts once however many times they toggled.
  • The report must not show the average of daily rates. Day 1 = 1 ÷ 1 = 100% and day 2 = 1 ÷ 3 = 33.3%, so their average of 66.7% would be wrong. The correct figure is 50%.
  • Total price: only U1, U2 and U3 could see it (U4 has no financial data). U1 and U2 have it on (default) and U3 turned it off, so the rate is 2 ÷ 3 = 66.7%, not 2 ÷ 4 = 50%.
  • Rounding: write down how the report rounds (e.g. 66.7% or 67%). The number must round from 2 ÷ 3.
